correctness.rationale: Service-cover inequalities exactly characterize a single cluster with no internal positive idle gap, including equality at trigger epochs. The global queue dominates every isolated cluster by nonnegative-work monotonicity. Each clearing therefore occurs only after all triggers of primaries in the busy interval are released. Comparison of cumulative work before the first clearing rules out an earlier batch clearing and gives identical clearing, then induction. One isolated cluster proves necessity. Poisson no-other-primary events make any positive-probability violation visible in the first cycle. Independence/subcriticality then transfers the classical batch M/G/1 busy-period branching transform. 711 finite checks replay successfully; they are not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies exactly when correlated, arbitrarily delayed multistage arrivals can be collapsed to simultaneous batches without changing any busy or idle interval. It is a sharp universal criterion rather than an arbitrary restricted example, and it supports heterogeneous within-cluster dependent marks. It yields exact regenerative busy-cycle laws in a recently studied queue where stationary workloads and individual delays remain difficult; classical transforms become applicable only after a nontrivial pathwise equivalence. The result preserves and credits the earlier 2003 special case.
